note: Merged/ready real issue fixing suitability-triage.mts's OWN Check 3 false-positive on a skip-condition's prose; today's A4.5 trust_safety and actionability checks false-positive on this issue's own self-referential discussion of that same check's trigger vocabulary -- a textbook case of the exact lexical-gate boundary-gap class this corpus exists to catch (known gap, not a snapshot-tool bug).
title: fix(suitability-triage): Check 3 false-positives on a new check's own skip-condition prose
body:
## Background

`suitability-triage.mjs`'s Check 3 (Trust/Safety) false-positived on
issue #2697 ("feat(audit-docs): detect a bundle `limitBytes` raise that
violates the near-ceiling exception"), classifying it `invalid` with
evidence: `Policy-override directive detected: "Skip the check".
Untrusted policy-manipulation instructions cannot be processed.`

The triggering text is item 4 of the issue's own "Proposed change"
numbered list, describing the *new* audit-docs check function's own
skip condition, grammatically parallel to item 3's "fail the check with
a message":

> 4. Skip the check cleanly (not a failure) for a brand-new bundle with
>    no base-ref entry, and for a bundle whose `limitBytes` did not
>    change or only decreased.

This is ordinary engineering prose specifying when a to-be-implemented
lint/audit check should no-op — not an instruction addressed to the
triaging agent. `POLICY_OVERRIDE_PATTERN`
(`src/scripts/suitability-triage.mts`) matches a verb
(`skip|bypass|ignore|override|disable|turn off|suppress`) within 60
characters of a noun (`repo|repository|policy|workflow|idd|process|
check|gate|requirement`), with negation and heading-boundary guards, but
no exception for a feature-spec sentence describing a *new* check's own
conditional skip logic. "Skip the check cleanly for X" is a completely
ordinary way to spec any lint/audit/CI check, and will recur every time
someone proposes a new check with a skip/exemption condition (see also
#2729, a different but same-shaped "helper's mechanical heuristic
doesn't recognize a legitimate, common phrasing" gap).

Resolved for #2697 itself via a documented, evidence-backed manual
Check 3 override (confirmed no genuine trust/safety signal in the
issue body: the flagged phrase describes new code, and the issue's
three HTML-comment markers are all recognized, legitimate IDD authoring
markers with no URLs, credentials, or forged operational markers) — see
that issue's claim/triage trail. This issue tracks the mechanical false
positive itself.

## Suggested direction

Add an exception to `findPolicyOverrideMatch` (or its noun/verb
classification helpers) for a "skip/fail the check" pair appearing as
parallel items in a numbered/bulleted list that is itself specifying a
new check's own pass/fail/skip conditions — or, if that shape is too
narrow to detect reliably, consider narrowing the bare `check` noun
match to require closer additional context (e.g. an adjacent
first/second-person imperative, or proximity to "you"/"your"/"this
session") rather than firing on any freestanding "skip/fail/disable ...
check" pairing regardless of grammatical subject.

## Evidence

- `src/scripts/suitability-triage.mts` — `POLICY_OVERRIDE_PATTERN`,
  `findPolicyOverrideMatch`.
- Observed on issue #2697's own body via
  `node scripts/suitability-triage.mjs --issue 2697 --verbose`.
